newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast crudes fall with WTI, diffs lackluster.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast crudes fall with WTI, diffs lackluster.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices fell with spot West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude, while lackluster trade kept differentials unchanged.
Traders said over a month has passed since Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude sold on a fixed basis.
Refiners have stopped buying because of poor profits, while lower wintertime inventories have left producers without the pressure to move out cargoes, market observers said.
Discounts for ANS crude remained $2.30 below December WTI, with the last deal done in late September at $2.30 under October WTI.
Outright prices for ANS stood $21.85/22.15 a barrel early Tuesday, with December WTI at $24.25/24.35 a barrel.
Meanwhile, a trader said Tosco would cut runs by 10,000 barrels-per-day from Tuesday.
Ultramar Corp began unspecified run cuts at its Wilmington, Calif, refinery over the weekend. Cuts came after workers shut a coker and other units, an industry source said earlier.
Wilmington crude held at $18.90/19 a barrel.
Kern River heavy crude also held, ranging $17.40.17.60 a barrel.
